who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code, dst-1113
what: The test fails about one run in twenty with `round N: a read allocated Used { allocations: 2, bytes: 2080, largest: 2048 }` (N was 510 and 452). On blaze-vm, `cargo +nightly-2026-10-27 test -p tt --lib`: the unported tree 398ae458e8 failed 1 of 22 runs, the tree with tt`s Hegel tests ported (062b5c63d8) 1 of 22. Alone (`-- --exact`) it passed.
cost: a red run of a port that did not touch the test, and 40 runs to show it was there before
cause: not established. The test skips a round when one of its texts is already interned (`Symbol::find`), and the interner is the process`s, written by the tests running beside it, so which damaged bytes each round reads depends on thread timing; for some damage `TopSubtree::read_wire` allocates 2080 bytes, past the test`s bound of four times the wire`s length.
whys: the test is not a function of its inputs: it reads state other tests write; and the bound it asserts does not hold for every damaged input, which a fixed seed with a timing-dependent path only sometimes reaches
class: a test whose path depends on process-wide state shared with parallel tests
prevention: draw the damage from a blaze-sim tape with an interner of the test`s own (or texts no other test makes), so the failing damage is found every run and shrunk; then fix the reader`s allocation or the bound; not built
workaround: none taken; the port was judged against the base tree`s rate
